narrativeReportMd:
# MedicationStatement R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`MedicationStatement` has high-impact local breaking changes. The canonical resource identity is stable, but common R4 instances are not wire- or validation-compatible with R6 because status semantics changed, several elements were removed/renamed/merged, CodeableReference replaced choice and code/reference patterns, and dosage changed from a repeating `Dosage` array to a singular `DosageDetails` object.

## Scope
This report covers the base resource StructureDefinition and directly relevant local terminology/datatype references. Inherited base-artifact changes and search parameters are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
The largest theme is semantic refactoring: R4 `status` represented medication-use state, while R6 `status` represents recording lifecycle and `adherence` represents taking/not-taking state. The second theme is representation refactoring: `medication[x]`, `reasonCode/reasonReference`, and `dosage` changed wire shape. The third theme is reference-domain change: `context` became `encounter`, `partOf` lost targets, and `basedOn` disappeared.

## Highest-impact findings
Highest-impact findings are status/adherence, dosage, medication CodeableReference, removed `basedOn`, and merged reasons. These affect validators, generated models, FHIRPath/code paths, and clinical interpretation.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for status/adherence mapping, dosage transformation, removed workflow links, EpisodeOfCare contexts, removed partOf targets, and category terminology.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several changes are understandable model improvements, but deprecated aliases, transitional value sets, or official cross-version ConceptMaps would have reduced migration risk.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze DosageDetails/Dosage, CodeableReference, DomainResource inherited changes, MedicationStatement SearchParameters, and a status/adherence ConceptMap separately.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicationStatement` has high-impact local breaks. The top concerns are status/adherence semantics, dosage redesign, and removed/merged workflow/reason/context elements. The main uncertainty is the lack of official cross-version mapping guidance.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration requires explicit transforms for status/adherence, medication CodeableReference, reason CodeableReference, dosage DosageDetails, and removed workflow/context links. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy for nuanced adherence, effectiveTiming, multiple categories/sources, author, and DosageDetails.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural changes because they come directly from local StructureDefinitions and CodeSystems. Confidence is medium for clinical mapping recommendations because official diffs, narrative rationale, terminology expansions, and cross-version ConceptMaps were not available.

findings.title: MedicationStatement.status changed from medication-use status to recording status

oldState.summary: Required modifier code bound to R4 medication-statement-status: active, completed, entered-in-error, intended, stopped, on-hold, unknown, not-taken.

changedCodes.oldMeaning: Some actions implied by the statement may have occurred.
changedCodes.newMeaning: The statement was entered in error and is not valid.
changedCodes.changeSummary: The surviving code has a tighter recording-validity meaning.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Comparison used local CodeSystem concept lists rather than a terminology server expansion.

semanticText.definition: R4 describes the patient/source judgement about the state of medication use.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `status` mixed statement lifecycle and medication-taking state.

newState.summary: Required modifier code bound to R6 medication-statement-status: recorded, entered-in-error, draft.

binding.description: Recording status of the medication statement.

semanticText.definition: A code representing the status of recording the medication statement.
semanticText.comment: R6 says MedicationStatement.adherence should be used for patient adherence.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 `status` is a recording-lifecycle field; medication-taking state moves to `adherence.code`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because `status` is mandatory and required-bound, common R4 instances with `active`, `completed`, `stopped`, `on-hold`, `unknown`, `not-taken`, or `intended` fail R6 validation. Runtime logic that used `status` to infer whether a patient is taking a medication must be redesigned around `status` plus `adherence.code`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Mis-mapping medication-taking state can change clinical interpretation of a medication list.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate statement recording lifecycle from patient adherence/medication-use state.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: A less-breaking design could have retained the R4 medication-use `status` and added a separate recording-lifecycle element, or temporarily accepted legacy status codes while adding `adherence`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating record lifecycle from patient medication-use/adherence state is a reasonable R6 goal, and the old required modifier `status` mixed those concerns. Because the field is mandatory and safety-relevant, a clean semantic split is plausibly worth substantial migration cost. The break is not fully unavoidable, though, because R6 could have used a transitional base design that retained the old status shape while adding clearer lifecycle/adherence structure.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest base-design alternative would have kept the R4 `status` codes valid and introduced a distinct recording-lifecycle element, or accepted legacy status codes as deprecated while new instances used `adherence`. That would preserve most R4 payloads, but it would make status semantics harder to validate and could leave two competing same-resource ways to communicate taking/not-taking state indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves many R4 instances, but leaves a required modifier status with legacy semantics and risks duplicate or ambiguous status/adherence representations.

evidence.detail: R4 status is required-bound to medication-statement-status|4.0.1.
R6 status is required-bound to medication-statement-status|6.0.0-ballot4.
R4 and R6 local code systems have different concept sets.
R6 redirects medication-taking/adherence state to MedicationStatement.adherence.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments isolate the status issue; complete instances also need medication and subject.

findings.narrativeMd: This is the central semantic break. R4 status values described whether the medication was active, stopped, on hold, not taken, and so on. R6 status values describe whether the statement record is recorded, draft, or entered in error, with medication-use state represented by `adherence.code`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 payloads with removed required-bound status codes are invalid in R6. R6 payloads with nuanced adherence codes such as `taking-as-directed` or `stopped-not-as-directed` cannot be losslessly represented by R4 `status` alone.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create an explicit mapping policy: most non-error R4 statements likely become R6 `status = recorded` plus an `adherence.code` derived from the old status. Review `intended`, `unknown`, and not-taking/on-hold cases manually or by profile-specific rules.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The semantic split is defensible, but deprecated aliases or an official ConceptMap would have reduced validation churn.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The package contains status-to-resource-status ConceptMaps for each release, not an R4-to-R6 status/adherence ConceptMap.

findings.title: statusReason was removed and partially replaced by adherence.reason

oldState.summary: Top-level repeatable CodeableConcept reason for current status.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed multiple top-level status reasons.

newState.summary: Nested singular CodeableConcept reason under adherence; adherence.code is mandatory when adherence is present.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 carries the reason under the adherence backbone and allows only one `adherence.reason`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances containing `statusReason` use a removed element. Mapping to R6 is not always lossless because multiple reasons must fit one `adherence.reason` and the parent requires an adherence code.

justification.inferredGoal: Align reasons with the new adherence model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain top-level repeatable `statusReason` with a revised definition tied to adherence/use status, instead of removing it and reducing the reason cardinality to one.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving status reasons closer to the new adherence model is understandable, but the local evidence does not show that the old top-level path or `0..*` cardinality had to be removed. The R6 goal could largely be met by clarifying the old element's meaning while adding `adherence.code`, so the level of breakage appears avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base design could keep `MedicationStatement.statusReason` as `0..*` CodeableConcept, update its definition to mean reason for current adherence/use state, and optionally discourage it in favor of a newer pattern. That preserves R4 instances and multiple reasons with only moderate modeling untidiness.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps a less tidy legacy name and a top-level reason outside the adherence backbone, but avoids raw instance breakage and repeat-reason data loss.

evidence.detail: R4 has `statusReason` 0..* CodeableConcept.
R6 has `adherence.reason` 0..1 CodeableConcept.
R6 requires `adherence.code` 1..1 inside adherence.

examples.examplesMd: Multiple R4 reasons may need consolidation or extension preservation.

findings.narrativeMd: `statusReason` is not simply renamed. It moves under a new adherence container, changes maximum cardinality from many to one, and becomes dependent on `adherence.code`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Raw R4 instances with `statusReason` are invalid in R6. R6 can carry one adherence reason, while R4 can carry multiple status reasons.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map only after deciding the R4 status-to-adherence code. Preserve multiple reasons via combined text, extension, or manual review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The move is coherent with the new model, but keeping a deprecated repeatable top-level field or repeatable nested reason would have been more compatible.

findings.title: basedOn was removed

oldState.summary: 0..* Reference(MedicationRequest|CarePlan|ServiceRequest) indicating a plan, proposal, or order fulfilled by the statement.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 has no local element with the same fulfillment semantics.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance with `basedOn` is invalid in R6 unless transformed. The removed link can be important to order/plan fulfillment and audit workflows.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep optional `basedOn` in the base resource, possibly deprecated or with narrower guidance, while recommending newer workflow/provenance links where appropriate.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred simplification goal may be reasonable, but removing an optional workflow link creates a direct validation break and no exact R6 replacement is evident in the local definitions. Preserving the old element with guidance would have met compatibility needs with limited long-term burden.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have left `MedicationStatement.basedOn` as `0..* Reference(MedicationRequest|CarePlan|ServiceRequest)` and marked it deprecated or constrained by profiles. That would preserve order/plan fulfillment links in existing R4 data while allowing implementations to migrate toward `derivedFrom`, Provenance, Task, or other workflow patterns.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retains an older workflow-link field and possible overlap with other linkage mechanisms, but the compatibility cost is low because the element is optional.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `basedOn` 0..* Reference(MedicationRequest|CarePlan|ServiceRequest).
R6 contains no `MedicationStatement.basedOn` element.

examples.examplesMd: A possible `derivedFrom` mapping preserves a reference but not necessarily fulfillment semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: The R4 workflow link to the plan/proposal/order being fulfilled is absent in R6. This is a direct element-removal break and a semantic migration issue.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 JSON/XML containing `basedOn` is invalid in R6. R6-to-R4 representability is not the main issue because the R6 element was removed rather than expanded.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory uses and map deliberately to `derivedFrom`, Provenance, Task, an extension, or another workflow artifact only when semantics are confirmed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping optional `basedOn` as deprecated would have avoided a raw validation break while still allowing model evolution.

findings.title: medication[x] was replaced by medication CodeableReference

oldState.summary: Required choice: CodeableConcept or Reference(Medication), serialized as medicationCodeableConcept or medicationReference.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used choice element wire names.

newState.summary: Required CodeableReference targeting Medication, serialized as medication.concept and/or medication.reference.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 includes the general medication-codes value set and SNOMED CT 787481004; full SNOMED expansion was not performed.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses CodeableReference rather than a FHIR choice element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 payloads use `medicationCodeableConcept` or `medicationReference`, neither of which is an R6 element. Generated models change from a polymorphic choice to a wrapper datatype.

justification.inferredGoal: Adopt CodeableReference for concept-or-reference medication identity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 `medication[x]` choice as a deprecated transition path, or add a parallel CodeableReference element while keeping the old choice valid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using CodeableReference for concept-or-reference medication identity is a coherent R6 modeling goal, especially because it can carry concept and reference together. A less-breaking base design exists, but it would keep two same-resource representations of the required medication fact, which is a material long-term tradeoff.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base alternative is not merely a transform; it would be to keep `medicationCodeableConcept`/`medicationReference` valid for a transition or introduce a new CodeableReference field alongside them. That reduces migration churn but risks persistent disagreement between legacy and new medication representations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve old wire format, but creates duplicate medication-identity representations and complicates validation, serializers, generated models, and long-term interoperability.

evidence.detail: R4 medication is CodeableConcept or Reference(Medication).
R6 medication is CodeableReference targeting Medication.
R6 medication value set wraps medication-codes and adds SNOMED CT 787481004.

examples.examplesMd: R4 choice arms map to `medication.concept` or `medication.reference`; R6 content with both needs policy.

findings.narrativeMd: The business meaning remains medication identity, but the element is no longer a choice. This creates hard wire-format and codegen breaks.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 choice properties are invalid in R6. R6 CodeableReference can carry nested content that is not cleanly reducible to one R4 choice arm.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `medicationCodeableConcept` to `medication.concept` and `medicationReference` to `medication.reference`; update generated SDK accessors and serializers.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The datatype change is understandable but could have been eased by compatibility transforms or aliases.

findings.title: context was renamed/narrowed to encounter and EpisodeOfCare was removed

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed encounter or episode context.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Encounter references can be renamed, but any R4 `context` field is invalid in raw R6 and EpisodeOfCare context has no base R6 target.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify that local context is specifically an encounter.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `context` with Encounter and EpisodeOfCare targets, clarifying that Encounter is the preferred interpretation, or retain it as a deprecated alias when adding `encounter`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying that the common context is an Encounter is reasonable, but the R4 `context` name and EpisodeOfCare target could have been retained while documenting the preferred R6 use. The local artifacts do not show why raw compatibility had to be broken for this rename and target narrowing.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 base design could continue to allow `MedicationStatement.context` as `Reference(Encounter|EpisodeOfCare)` with updated wording, or add `encounter` while keeping `context` deprecated. This would preserve R4 instances, including EpisodeOfCare contexts, while still steering new implementations toward Encounter-specific use.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Leaves a broader and less precise legacy name/target set, but preserves valid R4 contexts with modest validation and documentation cost.

evidence.detail: R4 context targets Encounter and EpisodeOfCare.
R6 encounter targets Encounter only.

examples.examplesMd: Only Encounter contexts have a direct R6 base mapping.

findings.narrativeMd: `context` appears to become `encounter`, but the removal of EpisodeOfCare makes this more than a property rename.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `context` is invalid in R6. Encounter targets can be renamed; EpisodeOfCare targets require extension or another related artifact.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename Encounter contexts to `encounter`. Preserve EpisodeOfCare context via extension, Provenance, CarePlan/Account linkage, or local policy.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The clearer name could have been introduced while retaining EpisodeOfCare compatibility.

findings.title: partOf targets were narrowed and the summary flag changed

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed several parent event types and included `partOf` in summary output.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 retains only Procedure and MedicationStatement targets.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances pointing `partOf` at MedicationAdministration, MedicationDispense, or Observation fail R6 reference target validation. Summary responses may also stop carrying this linkage.

justification.inferredGoal: Possibly restrict part-of relationships to more appropriate parent events.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 `partOf` target profiles in base R6 and use deprecation, warnings, or profile guidance to discourage targets considered semantically weak.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Narrowing `partOf` may reflect a reasonable desire for tighter event semantics, but the supplied definitions do not explain why MedicationAdministration, MedicationDispense, and Observation targets had to become invalid in the base resource. A less-breaking base design could have preserved those targets while documenting preferred alternatives.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept `partOf` as `Reference(MedicationAdministration|MedicationDispense|MedicationStatement|Procedure|Observation)` and introduced guidance or profile constraints for stricter use. That would preserve R4 data and allow gradual convergence, at the cost of weaker base validation and possible continued use of broad parent links.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old references but keeps a broader parent-event domain and may perpetuate ambiguous part-of relationships or summary-response expectations.

evidence.detail: R4 allows MedicationAdministration, MedicationDispense, MedicationStatement, Procedure, Observation.
R6 allows only Procedure and MedicationStatement.
R4 summary=true.
R6 summary=false.

findings.narrativeMd: The element remains, but its reference domain is substantially narrower and it is no longer a summary element.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Only R4 instances using removed target types are invalid. Generated reference target unions and summary payload expectations must change.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Keep Procedure and MedicationStatement references. Review removed targets and move them to `derivedFrom`, `relatedClinicalInformation`, Provenance, or extensions only when semantically appropriate.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The narrower domain could have been introduced by profiles or warnings while retaining the old base targets.

findings.title: reasonCode and reasonReference were merged into reason CodeableReference

oldState.summary: Separate repeating reasonCode CodeableConcept and reasonReference Reference(Condition|Observation|DiagnosticReport).

newState.summary: Single repeating CodeableReference reason targeting Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, or Procedure.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses one CodeableReference list and adds Procedure as a target.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 reason fields no longer exist in R6. R6 Procedure reasons and combined CodeableReference concept/reference entries are not losslessly representable in R4.

justification.inferredGoal: Unify coded and referenced reasons using CodeableReference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` as deprecated aliases, or add `reason` CodeableReference in parallel while retaining the old fields.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Unifying coded and referenced reasons with CodeableReference is a reasonable R6 model improvement and also permits the added Procedure target. The less-breaking base alternative would require keeping parallel old and new representations of the same reason facts, which is a substantial interoperability and validation tradeoff.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base-design alternative could leave `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` valid and introduce `reason` as the preferred CodeableReference form. It would reduce R4-to-R6 breakage, but implementers would need rules to prevent or reconcile duplicate reasons and to preserve ordering and concept/reference pairing.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances, but creates duplicate reason representations, ordering ambiguity, and possible divergence between coded and referenced reasons.

evidence.detail: R4 has reasonCode 0..* CodeableConcept.
R4 has reasonReference 0..* Reference(Condition|Observation|DiagnosticReport).
R6 has reason 0..* CodeableReference with Procedure added.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 collapses the parallel R4 reason fields into one CodeableReference list and expands the reference domain.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` are invalid in R6 until transformed. R6 Procedure reasons have no R4 reasonReference target.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map R4 coded reasons to `reason.concept` and referenced reasons to `reason.reference`; define policy for ordering and for R6 Procedure reasons in backward conversion.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The merged model is cleaner, but aliases or a formal cross-version transform would have reduced breakage.

findings.title: dosage changed from repeating Dosage array to singular DosageDetails object

oldState.summary: 0..* Dosage, serialized as an array in JSON.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `dosage` could repeat and each repetition was a Dosage.

newState.summary: 0..1 DosageDetails; when present, DosageDetails.renderedInstruction is 1..1 markdown.

constraints.human: DosageDetails.renderedInstruction is required by the datatype.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 `dosage` is a single DosageDetails object with rendered instructions and optional steps/components.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 `dosage` array is not the R6 wire shape, multiple repetitions exceed R6 max=1, and a migrated R6 DosageDetails must supply renderedInstruction.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent a complete dosage course as one rendered instruction plus structured steps.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add a new `dosageDetails` element or transition choice while retaining the R4 repeating `dosage` Dosage array in base R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 DosageDetails model appears to pursue a clinically important goal: one complete rendered instruction plus structured steps. Existing R4 dosage arrays are common and safety-sensitive, but retaining them alongside DosageDetails would create material ambiguity about the authoritative dosage instruction. That makes the break probably justified despite high migration cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `MedicationStatement.dosage` as `0..* Dosage` and added an optional `dosageDetails` or choice-based transition path. This would preserve R4 wire format, but systems would need robust reconciliation rules whenever both old and new dosage forms appear, and deprecated dosage representations might persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve old dosage arrays, but two dosage models for the same patient-safety content could conflict and indefinitely burden validation, rendering, and clinical review.

evidence.detail: R4 dosage is 0..* Dosage.
R6 dosage is 0..1 DosageDetails.
R6 DosageDetails.renderedInstruction is mandatory 1..1 markdown.

dosage.renderedInstruction: Take one tablet daily. Then take two tablets daily.

examples.examplesMd: The example is schematic; clinical review is needed for actual dosage text generation and step ordering.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a major validation, serialization, codegen, and clinical migration issue. R4 `dosage` is an array of Dosage; R6 `dosage` is one DosageDetails object with required rendered instructions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `dosage: [...]` are not raw-valid R6. Multiple R4 dosages must be merged, and R6 DosageDetails cannot be losslessly reduced to R4 repeated Dosage in all cases.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Build a dedicated dosage transform. Generate or review `renderedInstruction`, preserve dose/timing data in steps/components where possible, and test multi-step and safety-sensitive cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A transition element or compatibility alias would have reduced risk, but the R6 model appears to favor a single structured dosage course.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Datatype-level Dosage and DosageDetails breaking changes should be analyzed separately.

findings.title: category became repeatable and switched to medicationrequest-category with weaker binding

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed one category from a statement-specific preferred value set.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 element definition says the committee expects to revisit these codes.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 allows multiple categories and uses the MedicationRequest category value set as example strength.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Forward migration is structurally safe because cardinality widened and binding weakened. Backward conversion can lose extra categories and category terminology expectations differ.

justification.inferredGoal: Align statement category with medication request categories and allow multiple categories.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because R6 widens cardinality and weakens the binding, preserving R4 category instances structurally.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing multiple categories and using an example binding is forward-compatible for R4 instances, so this finding is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue. The R6 terminology remains somewhat unsettled, so the model change is best treated as probably reasonable rather than definitively justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because R4 `category` content remains valid in R6, backward-compatible alternative analysis does not apply in the calibration sense. Migration concern is mainly backward conversion: multiple R6 categories and request-category codes may need selection, mapping, or extension preservation when converting to R4.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is R6-to-R4 and semantic/terminology ambiguity, not a forward base-design break.

evidence.detail: R4 category is 0..1 preferred-bound to medication-statement-category.
R6 category is 0..* example-bound to medicationrequest-category.
R4 statement category includes patientspecified; R6 request category includes discharge.

examples.examplesMd: Multiple R6 categories cannot fit R4 max=1.

findings.narrativeMd: This is not a forward hard break, but it is material for round-trip and conformance because cardinality and terminology expectations changed.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 category content remains structurally acceptable in R6. R6 multiple categories exceed R4 cardinality and may use category codes outside old statement-category conventions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Copy old category values forward; for backward conversion choose a primary category or preserve extras via extension. Avoid assuming `patientspecified` and `discharge` are equivalent.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A transition binding or ConceptMap would have made the semantic shift clearer.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Recheck this area against later R6 builds because the R6 definition explicitly says category codes may be revisited.

findings.title: effective[x] adds Timing as an allowed type

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 effective timing was a point/partial date or interval.

newState.summary: 0..1 choice of dateTime, Period, or Timing.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 can express richer Timing patterns.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding Timing is forward-compatible for R4 data but R6 `effectiveTiming` cannot be represented in base R4.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow richer timing patterns for medication-use assertions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because adding `Timing` preserves existing R4 `dateTime` and `Period` instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This is an additive type widening in the forward direction. It supports richer timing assertions without invalidating R4 instances, so the calibration question about a less-breaking R6 base design is not applicable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R4-to-R6 compatibility is already preserved by keeping the existing choice types. R6-to-R4 conversion needs separate policy for `effectiveTiming`, but an extension or approximation for older releases is a conversion mitigation rather than a base R6 alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The only material tradeoff is lossy R6-to-R4 conversion for new `effectiveTiming` content.

evidence.detail: R4 supports dateTime and Period.
R6 supports dateTime, Period, and Timing.

findings.narrativeMd: This is an additive R6 feature with backward conversion risk.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `effectiveDateTime` and `effectivePeriod` still map forward. R6 `effectiveTiming` is invalid in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Leave old values unchanged. For R6-to-R4, approximate, move to dosage/extension, or require manual review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The addition is reasonable; representability risk should be handled by conversion guidance.

findings.title: informationSource became repeatable with Device/Group targets and author was added

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had one information source and no local author element.

newState.summary: informationSource is 0..* and adds Device/Group; author is new 0..1 Reference including Device.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 distinguishes source(s) from the responsible author.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Forward migration is additive, but R6 can carry multiple sources, Device/Group sources, and author information that base R4 cannot represent in MedicationStatement.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate authorship from information source and support device/group sources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because `informationSource` is widened and `author` is optional.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating authorship from information source and allowing additional source targets is a reasonable additive refinement. Existing R4 instances remain valid with respect to these fields, so this is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The R6 base design already preserves R4-to-R6 compatibility for this area. Backward conversion may need a primary-source rule plus Provenance or extensions for additional source/author content, but those are down-conversion mitigations rather than less-breaking R6 base alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is lossy R6-to-R4 conversion for multiple sources, Device/Group sources, and author, not forward breakage.

evidence.detail: R4 informationSource is 0..1 and lacks Device/Group targets.
R6 informationSource is 0..* and adds Device/Group.
R6 adds author 0..1.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds provenance richness without breaking R4 instances moving forward, but backward conversion can be lossy.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 single source still maps forward. R6 multiple/device/group source or author content has no base R4 MedicationStatement slot.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For backward conversion, choose a primary R4 informationSource and preserve the rest in Provenance or extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This is a reasonable additive model improvement; conversion guidance is still needed.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, baseDefinition, and abstract=false are stable; R6 file exists at the expected path.
No local MedicationStatement-specific invariants were added, removed, or changed. Root `dom-*` changes are inherited and out of scope.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value constraints were found.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex constraints were found.
`MedicationStatement.status` remains a modifier; no existing local non-inherited element changed modifier status.
No local slicing was found in either StructureDefinition.
`subject` remains Reference(Patient|Group) and `derivedFrom` remains Reference(Resource). Material target changes are reported separately.

Major wire-shape changes were found for medication, reason, and dosage. Stable same-name elements such as identifier, subject, dateAsserted, derivedFrom, and note showed no material wire-shape change.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Resource metadata changed from draft/trial-use/FMM3 to active/normative/FMM4
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is artifact metadata, not an instance content rule.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance programs may care that R6 is normative/FMM4, while the supplied package is still a ballot build marked not for publication.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: relatedClinicalInformation was added
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element is optional, so R4 instances do not need new content to validate in R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 data using this element is not directly representable in base R4 MedicationStatement and may need an extension or related artifact.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly carries mustSupport=false on many base elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Explicit false does not impose a new support obligation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Profile-level MustSupport must still be compared separately.
